Abstract
Introduction: Globally dementia is a growing public health problem, with over 135,000 people in Nepal living with dementia. Nepal lacks national and community-based data on dementia prevalence. This study aims to determine the dementia risk in Nepal and assess the effects of age, sex, and geographical location on disease prevalence. Chi-squared tests and multiple logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess the effects.
Results: 53.7% (501) participants had cognitive impairment or risk of dementia, with slightly higher rates in women (56.5%) than men (51.7%). Cognitive impairment prevalence increases with age and region, with hilly and mountainous areas and low-lying regions having a greater geographic effect.
